name: KernSmooth
resume: All seven public functions are done: bkde, bkde2D, bkfe, dpih, dpik, dpill, and locpoly. bkde2D loads the Rust crate lbtwod. dpill loads blkest, cp, rlbin, sdiag, and sstdiag, and calls locpoly. sdiag and sstdiag use linpack. Density binning still uses linbin. Kernel weights and the FFT use NumPy.

functions.name: bkde
functions.done: Binned kernel density estimate. Signature matches KernSmooth::bkde and returns x and y. Kernel weights, default bandwidth, and FFT are Python on NumPy. Bin counts come from the linbin crate.

check.case: 10,000 standard normal points, normal kernel, gridsize 401

proof.r:
x <- scan("bkde-sample.txt", quiet=TRUE)
one <- function() KernSmooth::bkde(x)
invisible(one())
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
median(elapsed) * 1000
proof.python:
import statistics
import time

import numpy as np
from kernsmooth import bkde

sample = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=10_000)
np.savetxt("bkde-sample.txt", sample, fmt="%.17g")

def one():
    bkde(sample)

one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
statistics.median(elapsed)

functions.name: bkde2D
functions.done: Two-dimensional binned kernel density estimate. Signature matches KernSmooth::bkde2D and returns x1, x2, and fhat. Bin counts come from the lbtwod crate. The bivariate normal kernel and the 2D FFT stay in NumPy.

functions.name: dpill
functions.done: Direct plug-in bandwidth for local linear regression. Signature matches KernSmooth::dpill and returns one number. Pairs are binned with rlbin. Blocked quartic fits come from blkest and cp. Smoother diagonals come from sdiag and sstdiag. Pilot smooths use locpoly.

proof.r:

y <- geyser$waiting
one <- function() KernSmooth::dpill(x, y)
invisible(one())
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
median(elapsed) * 1000

functions.name: locpoly
functions.done: Local polynomial density and regression estimate. Signature matches KernSmooth::locpoly and returns x and y. Density bin counts come from the existing linbin crate. Regression bin counts come from rlbin. The fit comes from locpol, which calls linpack.
